newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao wins reprieves in two court cases.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao wins reprieves in two court cases.

text.p: Former Indian Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao won temporary respite from arrest on Monday when courts deferred rulings in two criminal cases that have shaken the governing coalition and financial markets.
A New Delhi High Court judge said he would rule later in the week on a request by Rao for legal protection against arrest in a seven-year-old forgery case.
The Supreme Court reserved judgement on a request by police that a hearing into a $100,000 criminal cheating case be shifted from a crowded local courtroom to a more secure location.
Until the two courts pass judgement on the requests, Rao will be spared arrest.

Rao, who was prime minister from mid-1991 until last May when his Congress Party went down to humiliating defeat in general elections, resigned as party leader on September 21 when a judge upheld a summons in the 13-year-old cheating case.
As the legal net tightened around Rao, pressure has mounted on the 75-year-old politician to quit as head of Congress's parliamentary delegation.

On Sunday, Rao's former finance minister, Manmohan Singh, was named to the party's main decision-making body, stirring speculation that he was being groomed to take over as head of the parliamentary group.

The turmoil within Congress, which has led India for all but four years since independence in 1947, has sent shivers through financial markets, which anticipate trouble for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority government.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index plunged 98.86 points, or 3.19 percent, to 3,002.41 points on Monday, closing a whisker above the psychological threshold of 3,000.
"Political worries are pulling down the market," said Sunil Kothari of brokers Nagindas S. Kothari in Bombay.
Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition depends on the support of Congress to survive in parliament against a challenge from the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Rao's replacement, 80-year-old Sitaram Kesri, has raised questions about the party's continuing support for Deve Gowda's minority coalition. Some of Deve Gowda's leftist allies have accused the government of shielding Rao from the law.

Last Friday, a Delhi court issued a warrant for Rao's arrest in the forgery case. Federal police claim Rao was part of a conspiracy in 1989 to use forged documents to defame a rival politician. Rao has not commented publicly on the case.

On Friday, Rao won a temporary reprieve by requesting anticipatory, or pre-emptive, bail, which amounts to legal protection against arrest. High Court Judge S.K. Mahajan said he would rule on the request on Tuesday or Wednesday.

If the High Court rejects Rao's request, he was expected to appeal to the Supreme Court. If detained, Rao would be put in custody pending a hearing on the forgery case set for October 14, they said. Rao suffers from diabetes and heart trouble.

The Supreme Court deferred a decision on whether to move the venue of a hearing, set for Wednesday, at which Rao was scheduled to be charged with criminal conspiracy to cheat an expatriate businessman of $100,000 in 1983. Rao, who could be arrested at the hearing, says he is innocent.

The government asked that the hearing, which looked likely to be delayed, be moved to a cavernous government conference hall where security forces could protect Rao. It was not known when the court would rule.
The Supreme Court said on Monday that both the cheating and forgery cases should preferably be concluded within three months of their start.
